# Reunion Hackathon

> A 48-hour hackathon in Warsaw, 5–7 February 2027, for 100 Polish students and recent graduates of universities abroad. Theme: AI transformation. Free to take part, with selection by application. Organised by Global Polish Student Society (GPSS).

Status (13 October 2026): applications are not open yet; the form will appear on the website.

- Dates: 5–7 February 2027. Friday 16:00 registration, 17:00 opening gala, 20:00 coding starts; Saturday 12:00 pitching workshop; Sunday 15:30 closing gala.
- Place: Warsaw, Poland. The exact venue will be announced before applications open.
- Who: 100 places for Polish students and recent graduates of universities abroad, mainly computer science, AI/ML, engineering and data science.
- Tracks: AI for people, AI in business and AI in government (partner tracks), plus an open track for a partner's own challenge.
- Partners: four packages (Title Sponsor, Track Partner, Supporting Partner, Patron). Contact: maks.rokosz@globalpolsoc.com

## FAQ

- Who can apply? Polish students and graduates of universities abroad, mainly in computer science, AI/ML, engineering and data science; selection is based on applications, and the exact criteria will be published with the form.
- How much does it cost? Taking part is free; places are limited to 100.
- Do I need a team? No. You can apply solo, and teams can also form on site during the opening.
- Do I need to code? The core of the event is building a prototype, but good teams also need design and business skills; what counts is what you bring to the project.
- Do we work at night? Yes. The room is open round the clock, from the start on Friday at 20:00 until projects are submitted on Sunday.
- How does the pitch work? Each team has 3 minutes for the pitch and 2 minutes for questions from the jury; a pitching workshop runs on Saturday at noon.
- What language is the event in? Polish; some workshops and materials may be in English.
- Are travel and accommodation covered? Logistics will be shared with accepted participants.
